$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{artanh}⁡(2x-1)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡(2x-1)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{1-{(2x-1)}^{2}}\cdot {(2x-1)}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{1-(4{x}^{2}-4x+1)}\cdot 2 \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{4x-4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{4x(1-x)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x(1-x)}.\end{aligned}
$$
